description: Aluminium is a chemical element with symbol Al and atomic number 13. It is a post-transition metal in the boron group that forms compounds primarily in the +3 oxidation state. It has one stable isotope, 27Al, and is the third-most abundant element in Earth's crust after oxygen and silicon.
uses: Aluminium is used in transportation, engineering, construction, and packaging. Its high affinity for oxygen makes it suitable as a reducing agent in thermite reactions. It is also used in radiometric dating through the radioactivity of 26Al, and its excellent thermal and electrical conductivity makes it valuable for applications where these properties are needed.
characteristics: Aluminium has a density of 2.70 g/cm³, about one-third that of steel, making it much lighter than most common metals. It is soft, ductile, and malleable in pure form, with a silvery white to dull gray appearance and excellent light reflectivity. It is an excellent thermal and electrical conductor, nonmagnetic, and forms a protective oxide layer on its surface when exposed to air.
